note: The canonical game-install tree for every dataset and ring. DATA-GAP-REGISTER PROV-1/PROV-2.
Exports read the LIVE game installs directly. The repo keeps no .pigg snapshots: a snapshot
goes stale in place, shares its shard basename with the tree it was copied from, and so
cannot be told apart by name — which is how a month-old Thunderspy corpus nearly shipped.
Only 'exportable_ring' may produce a committed export; the other rings exist to be READ when
checking what a patch is about to do, never to be exported into the tree users get.
Each dataset lists every ROOT it has been seen at — one per workstation — and each ring names
only its SUBPATH inside that root. Roots vary by machine; ring layout does not. The root in
use is whichever one exists here; if two exist, resolution refuses rather than guesses, and
BIN_CRAWLER_ASSETS_HOST=<host label> picks one by name. Adding a machine means adding a root,
not editing paths, so no workstation's entry has to be traded away for another's.
Paths may be written home-relative (~/…). Rejected subpaths apply under EVERY root, so a trap
named once stays named on every machine — schema 1 named them absolutely, so a trap silently
stopped rejecting anything the moment the workstation changed.
Every archive here was verified byte-identical to what the committed manifests recorded
before the 2026-08-04 re-export, so the moves recorded here restated WHERE, never WHAT.

roots.note: macOS, installed by the LaunchCat launcher.

live.note: The only Homecoming data users may ever see.

open_beta.note: Open beta. Checked once a patch moves from closed to open beta.

closed_beta.note: Closed beta, despite the folder being named 'experimental'. Checked once a patch moves from development to closed beta.

rejected_subpaths.closedbeta: NOT the closed beta despite the name — the closed beta is the 'experimental' folder. Never export from here.
rejected_subpaths.issue24: An Issue-24 era snapshot (bin.pigg dated 2023-05-08) sitting beside the live rings. Not a Homecoming ring at all — it is the pre-fork retail corpus, so an export from here would be a different GAME, not a stale one. Byte-identical bin.pigg to the Sweet Tea 'piggs' decoy — the same unrelated corpus, and it resolves powers.bin just as convincingly. Never export from here.

roots.note: macOS copy of the Sweet Tea install.

live.note: Rebirth ships from the Sweet Tea install, alongside Thunderspy. Its shard is z_rebirth_bin.pigg, not bin.pigg.

rejected_subpaths.rebirth_test: Rebirth's test ring. Not tracked — Rebirth's major updates are infrequent and its user base small, so only live is followed (dev, 2026-08-01).
rejected_subpaths.piggs: A decoy: it resolves powers.bin but yields an unrelated corpus (12,169 files differ from live).
